subject: Post-demo: Cascade competitive trial — next steps & test schedule
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Cascade competitive trial — next steps & test schedule

Hi Lisa / Mike —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo and the proposed plan for the competitive trial so we have aligned expectations. High-level takeaways:

- Priority workloads: conversational search (multi-turn sessions) and a generator path for short-form responses (~16–64 tokens).
- Key concerns you raised: 95th-pct latency, cold-start behavior, and VPC/networking requirements.
- Hyperscaler baseline: you mentioned running an internal HypCloud endpoint for comparison — we will match that in the matrix.

Proposed next steps (suggested owners and timeline):
1) Trial scope & test matrix — we (Redwood) deliver a baseline matrix + configs by EOD Fri (Avery).
2) Credentials & automated harness — we provide short-lived trial credentials and a benchmark runner (Avery) by Mon 2/16.
3) Spike runs & daily sampling — run targeted cases (latency p50/p95, throughput, cost-per-1M tokens, KV-cache hit-rate) during week of 2/23.
4) Sync cadence — twice-weekly check-ins (Mon/Wed) during trial; final results and showback the week of 3/9.

Owners: Avery will lead execution and scripts; Laura will own pass/fail criteria and quality gating; I’ll be the primary contact for logistics and contract/trial paperwork.

Can you confirm the tentative start week (2/23) and whether HypCloud will be the baseline we should instrument? If you want, we can also include an on-prem/private runner as a fallback.

Attachments: I will send the trial matrix + config in the next message.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@cascade.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Cascade competitive trial — next steps & test schedule

Connor —

Appreciate the recap and the clear plan. 2/23 as a start week looks good on our end. A couple of clarifications before you send configs:

- Primary objectives: (1) end-to-end 95th-pct latency for multi-turn chat under realistic traffic, and (2) model output quality on our in-house prompt set. Latency is slightly higher priority.
- Security: we need to validate VPC peering and that no unencrypted token/trace data leaves our environment. Can you include the security contact for Redwood and a brief note on how logs/traces are handled?
- Baseline: yes, HypCloud is our current baseline. We will expose an instrumented endpoint; would be great if Redwood can run side-by-side tests on equivalent instance types (or specify what you consider an equivalent config).

Also, will you be able to capture KV cache hit-rate metrics for session flows? That’s an important factor for our expected cost savings.

If you can send the trial matrix and the exact list of metrics (and the short-run harness), we’ll review and confirm by Monday.

Thanks —
Lisa Park
Director, Platform Engineering | Cascade Solutions

On Fri, Feb 13, 2026 at 11:02 AM Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Attaching the proposed trial matrix (cascade-trial-matrix.xlsx) and the Redwood runner config (rdw-test-config.yaml).

Quick note on measurable success criteria so we have alignment before runs begin:

- Latency: target p95 < 250ms for small prompts (<=64 tokens) under the defined load profile.
- Cost: cost-per-1M tokens <= 0.7x HypCloud baseline on matched instance class (we’ll document baseline during instrumentation).
- Quality: for the provided prompt set, pass-rate >= 92% on your judged quality rubric (we’ll use blind sampling).
- Cache behavior: KV-cache hit-rate >= 60% on session-flows for a realistic distribution; report both hit-rate and effective token reduction.

If any of these need adjustment, call it out now — otherwise we’ll treat them as the acceptance gate at the end of the trial. Attached a short brief with the evaluation approach (neon-benchmarks-brief.pdf).

Fallbacks: if the hosted approach doesn’t meet latency | security needs, we discussed a scoped Private deployment to run inside your VPC — we can prepare an estimate once we have trial data.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Evals | Redwood Inference
